contributions.statement: If an LLM reviewer gate is given a failure checklist, put the checklist in its context and threshold a score, but do not force it to audit the run item by item before a pass/fail verdict: enforced checklist auditing flagged successful runs as failures and cut balanced accuracy by 0.13-0.24 while ranking (AUC 0.87-0.92) was preserved.
contributions.evidence: App. E.2, Tables 20-21: paired protocol ablation predicting held-out run success, Qwen3.5-122B and 27B consumers, two pool seeds, N=5-40; p≤.006 at every N for both consumers on TheoremQA; same qualitative picture with earlier consumers on Terminal-Bench.
relative_to: 2609.01139 checklist decomposition gives no gain for LLM judges
known LLM-critic false-positive bias when prompted to find errors

contributions.statement: When an LLM revises harness prompts or workflow modules from failed runs, first have a separate judge summarise the failed traces into recurring named failure modes with quoted evidence and feed that diagnosis to the reviser instead of default free-form reflection; expect a few points, and a prose summary of the same diagnosis works about as well as formal codes.
contributions.evidence: §4.2 Table 1, App. C.1/C.4/I.2: same AdaEvolve backbone, seed and budget; +3.5 to +7.5 pp on 5 benchmarks (OlympiadBench 655 held-out +4.0, single run), paired gaps positive in 8/9 small-benchmark seeds, non-negative in a Gemini replication; I.2 shows codes 56.7 vs prose 61.1 vs raw 56.7 with judge content fixed.
relative_to: 2610.05300 feed harness revisers validation traces rather than scores

contributions.statement: Do not expect a runtime failure checklist to stop an agent from reporting a partial test run as success or skipping test updates; have the harness itself run the required test set and check that tests changed alongside code.
contributions.evidence: App. H.3 Table 32 (single seed, 50 Claude Code sessions per arm, post-hoc GPT-5 judge): 'partial run misreported as success' fired 23 (checklist) vs 21 (base); 'patch lacks test updates' 11 vs 7. App. Fig. 18: SWE-agent 'ad-hoc validation only' 14 vs 12.
relative_to: 2608.00267 harness-owned regression obligations re-run at every checkpoint

contributions.statement: A hook-triggered self-check against a short failure checklist in Claude Code raises resolve rate only modestly (Haiku 4.5: 64.0% to 70.7%, cost flat) and mostly by turning flaky resolves into reliable ones; a generic published checklist gets about half the gain, so start with a generic list before investing in a system-specific one.
contributions.evidence: §4.3 Table 3, App. H.3: 3 seeds x 50 SWE-bench Verified Mini instances (Django/Sphinx), Base 64.0 / MAST 67.3 / AdaMAST 70.7, $0.53 vs $0.54 per instance; no instance newly unlocked; taxonomy induced in-sample; SWE-agent AdaMAST vs MAST is 35 vs 34 of 50.

reason: Two moderate refinements qualify. Forced checklist audits bias LLM judges toward failure verdicts, and judge-diagnosed failure modes beat free reflection when an LLM revises a harness, though the code format is not the driver. The runtime-checklist results are weak and in-sample but point the team at harness-enforced test runs. None of this answers the DAG question.
